blocks.text: What are the attributes of God according to Christianity?

Christians understand God's attributes as the perfections that describe who God is. Catholic theology teaches that these attributes are not separate parts added to God; they belong to His one, simple and perfect divine being.

Some attributes, such as infinity, eternity, immutability and omnipresence, belong to God in a way that creatures cannot possess. Others, such as love, goodness, wisdom and faithfulness, are reflected in creation and shared with creatures in a limited way.

blocks.title: In one sentence
blocks.text: God is infinitely perfect, eternal, unchanging, all-knowing, all-powerful, perfectly good and loving, and fully present to His creation.

Catholic theology distinguishes between communicable and incommunicable attributes. Incommunicable attributes belong to God alone, while communicable attributes are reflected in creatures in a limited way.

The Church also teaches divine simplicity: God's attributes are not separate components of His being. God is not partly loving, partly wise or partly good. His perfections belong to His one, unified divine essence.

blocks.title: Divine simplicity
blocks.text: God does not possess His attributes as separate parts. His divine perfections are united in His one and simple being.
Infinity
God is infinite in all His perfections. He has no limits, boundaries or restrictions in His being, knowledge, power or presence.
Eternity
God is eternal. He does not begin or cease to exist and transcends the succession of moments that characterizes created time.
Immutability
God does not change in His divine perfection, essence or truth. His unchanging nature does not prevent Him from freely acting in time and relating to His creatures.
Impassibility
God is not subject to involuntary suffering or external forces that would diminish His perfection. His love is freely given rather than compelled by need.
Simplicity
God is not composed of parts. His essence and existence are not divided into separate components, and His attributes are united in His one divine being.
Omnipresence
God is present everywhere. He is not limited by space and sustains His creation while remaining fully present to it.
Omniscience
God knows all things perfectly. His knowledge encompasses what is actual and possible, and nothing escapes His knowledge.
Omnipotence
God is all-powerful. His power is perfectly consistent with His nature, wisdom and goodness and is manifested in creation, providence and redemption.
Goodness
God is perfectly good and is the supreme source of all created goodness. Everything good in creation reflects His goodness.
Love
God is love itself. Divine love is not merely an emotion but belongs to God's very being and is perfectly expressed in the communion of Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
Wisdom
God perfectly knows how all things are ordered toward their proper ends. His wisdom is manifested in creation and in the work of salvation, and is perfectly revealed in Christ.
Justice
God is perfectly just, giving to each what is due according to His wisdom and goodness. Catholic teaching understands divine justice together with divine mercy.
Mercy
God is infinitely merciful. His mercy is His loving compassion toward those in need, especially sinners, and is revealed in forgiveness, healing and redemption.
Holiness
God is perfectly holy, completely separate from sin and evil and the source of all sanctity. His holiness calls believers to reverence and transformation.
Faithfulness
God is perfectly faithful. He keeps His promises and remains true to His covenant commitments, providing the foundation for Christian hope and trust.

Catholic theology teaches that the divine attributes belong fully to the one God in three Persons. The Father, Son and Holy Spirit do not divide the divine attributes between themselves; each Person fully possesses the one divine nature.

Therefore, God's omniscience, omnipotence, goodness and love are not three different versions of these attributes. They belong to the one divine essence shared eternally by the Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

sections.title: Knowing God Through Creation and Revelation

blocks.text: The Catholic Church teaches that God's attributes can be known through natural reason as well as divine revelation. Creation points beyond itself to its Creator and allows human reason to recognize realities such as power, wisdom and goodness.
The fuller knowledge of God's attributes comes through divine revelation, especially Sacred Scripture and the person of Jesus Christ. In Christ, the invisible God is made known in a definitive way.

blocks.title: Dei Verbum, 2
blocks.text: Through divine revelation, God chose to show forth and communicate himself and the eternal decisions of his will.

sections.title: What God's Attributes Mean for Christian Life

blocks.text: Knowing God's attributes is not merely an intellectual exercise. These truths shape prayer, worship, trust and moral life.

items: God's love encourages trust and intimacy in prayer.
God's holiness inspires reverence and the pursuit of sanctity.
God's justice calls believers to take sin and righteousness seriously.
God's mercy gives confidence in repentance, forgiveness and healing.
God's faithfulness provides a foundation for hope and perseverance.
God's wisdom encourages believers to trust His providence even when His purposes are not immediately understood.
God is infinite — He has no limits or boundaries.
God is eternal — He has no beginning or end.
God is immutable — He does not change in His divine perfection.
God is omnipresent — He is fully present to His creation.
God is omniscient — He knows all things perfectly.
God is omnipotent — He is all-powerful according to His perfect nature.
God is perfectly good, loving, wise, just, merciful, holy and faithful.
All divine attributes belong fully to the one God in three Persons.

blocks.text: The attributes of God provide a framework for understanding the infinite mystery of the Triune God. Catholic theology holds that these perfections are known through reason and revelation and are united in God's simple, perfect being. The more believers come to know who God is, the more they are invited to know, love and serve Him.

blocks.question: Are God's attributes separate parts of God?
blocks.answer: No. Catholic theology teaches divine simplicity: God's attributes are not separate components added to His being. They belong to His one, simple and perfect divine nature.

blocks.question: What is the difference between communicable and incommunicable attributes?
blocks.answer: Incommunicable attributes belong to God alone, such as infinity, eternity and immutability. Communicable attributes, such as goodness, love and wisdom, are reflected in creation and shared with creatures in a limited way.

blocks.question: Does God change when He responds to people?
blocks.answer: Catholic teaching holds that God is immutable in His divine nature. His free actions in time do not mean that His eternal perfection or essence changes.

blocks.question: Do the Father, Son and Holy Spirit have different attributes?
blocks.answer: No. The three divine Persons share one divine nature, so the divine attributes belong fully to the Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
